transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. To start, can you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

I came in because I keep hearing voices when nobody’s there. It’s clear, like somebody’s standing in my little studio, saying my name and telling me my work is being judged, even when the house is quiet.
Have you been using any alcohol, drugs, or other substances recently, especially around the time these voices started?
I’m not really sure what you mean by around the time they started. I haven’t noticed any connection like that.
Do you currently drink alcohol or use any recreational drugs, even occasionally?
I’m not sure. I don’t really know what you’d count as recreational drugs.
Have you ever used marijuana, cocaine, methamphetamine, or similar drugs, or drunk alcohol regularly, at any point in your life?
I don’t know... I can’t really say yes or no to all of that. I’m not sure what you need me to tell you.
How long have you been hearing these voices—days, weeks, or months?
About nine months, I think. The voices—and the feeling that my work is being watched—have been going on that long.
Over these past nine months, have you also noticed long stretches where you felt very sad, lost interest in things, or conversely felt unusually energetic, elated, or irritable?

Yeah. I’ll feel really bright, like I’m chosen and Greenville can’t even hold all the plans I have. Then I can turn around and snap at somebody over something small—like a client asking me to repeat myself.
During the times when you're not feeling unusually high or irritable—when your mood is more normal—do you still hear the voices or feel that your work is being watched?
Yes. There was a time when my energy had dropped and I was sleeping more normally, but the voices kept going. I still felt like people were judging me or tracking my work for weeks after that.

Thinking back over these 9 months, would you say the mood swings—the high energy or irritability—have been present for most of that time, or have there been longer stretches where your mood was normal but the voices and feelings of being watched continued?
Most of the time, I was either really wound up—making big plans, hardly sleeping, always doing something—or I was coming down from that. Even then, I didn’t feel like I was back to normal.
During that time when your energy had settled down and you were sleeping normally, how many weeks did that calmer period last before the mood swings started again?
It lasted several weeks, I think. My energy was down and I was sleeping more normally, but the voices and feeling like people were judging or tracking my work just kept going.
During those several calmer weeks, were you completely free of the high energy, irritability, or low mood, or did you still notice milder versions of those mood symptoms?
I mean, my energy had dropped and I was sleeping more normally for several weeks. But the voices kept going, and I still believed people were judging me or tracking my work.

During those several calmer weeks when your energy and sleep were more normal, did you notice any sadness, hopelessness, or loss of interest in things, or was your mood essentially normal aside from the voices and feeling watched?
I wasn’t really doing much. I’d sit for hours with my coffee going cold, not answer calls, skip the walking club. I didn’t even care to pick up my paintbrush.

During the times you felt depressed and low-energy, did you also notice any racing thoughts, elevated mood, or irritability happening at the very same time, or did the manic and depressive feelings always occur at separate, distinct periods?
I'm not sure. It all kind of runs together when I look back on it.

During that low, low-energy period when you weren't touching your paintbrush, did you also notice yourself feeling unusually energetic, talkative, or needing less sleep at the very same time—even for just a few days—or was that low period completely separate from your high-energy times?
I honestly can’t say for sure. Looking back, it’s hard for me to separate it all out—those times kind of blur together.

Think about just this past week: are you currently feeling low on energy and uninterested in things, or are you feeling unusually energetic, wound up, or irritable—or are both happening together right now?
This week I’ve been feeling really bright, like I’ve got all these plans and Greenville can’t hold me. But then I’ll snap at somebody over something little—like a client asking me to repeat myself.

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient reports auditory hallucinations and persecutory/referential delusions persisting continuously for 9 months. Concurrently, she describes manic-like symptoms (elevated mood, grandiosity, decreased need for sleep, irritability) and depressive symptoms (anhedonia, low energy, social withdrawal) that occur for the majority of the illness duration, consistent with a mood episode criterion. Critically, she endorses a distinct period of several weeks where mood symptoms settled (both manic and depressive symptoms diminished) yet the hallucinations and delusional beliefs of being watched/judged persisted, satisfying the requirement for psychotic symptoms occurring for at least 2 weeks in the absence of a prominent mood episode. This pattern—concurrent mood and psychotic symptoms for most of the illness plus a period of isolated psychosis—along with mood symptoms encompassing both manic and depressive features, supports schizoaffective disorder, bipolar type (F25.0) over schizophrenia (which requires psychosis to predominate without mood episodes) or a primary bipolar disorder with psychotic features (which would not have psychosis persisting after mood resolution for a full 2+ weeks). No clear substance use pattern was identified to account for the psychotic and mood symptoms, though the patient's inability to clarify substance history is noted as a limitation.

confirmed_symptoms: Auditory hallucinations (hearing voices saying her name, commenting on her work) present for 9 months
Delusional belief that her work is being judged/watched, persisting even when mood symptoms resolved
Psychotic symptoms continued for several weeks during a period of relatively normalized mood/energy
Elevated, grandiose mood ('chosen', grandiose plans city cannot hold)
Irritability (snapping at clients over minor things)
Decreased need for sleep during high periods
Anhedonia (loss of interest in painting, a previously valued activity)
Low energy and psychomotor slowing (sitting for hours, coffee going cold)
Social withdrawal (not answering calls, skipping walking club)

diagnostic_checklist.duration_verified: Psychotic symptoms present continuously for approximately 9 months; mood episodes (manic and depressive) present for the majority of this period, with a distinct multi-week period of psychosis without a full mood episode.
additional_requirements: Psychotic symptoms confirmed to persist for at least 2 weeks in the absence of prominent mood symptoms (satisfying schizoaffective criterion A2)
Mood symptoms (manic and depressive) confirmed to be present for the majority of the total illness duration (criterion B)
Substance use history could not be clearly ruled out or confirmed due to patient's uncertainty, but no clear temporal link to symptom onset was reported
